ideation.description: Feature ideation for pulse-brownfield-feature-demo. Context: `app/` is a fresh fork of nsidnev/fastapi-realworld-example-app (FastAPI + Postgres RealWorld/Conduit clone), documented in `app/FORK_NOTES.md`. Auth/error conventions are documented in `docs/decisions/0001-token-auth-scheme.md`. This board was reset (prior ideation/refinement/spec/sprint/card chains hard-deleted) so this pipeline can be authored fresh and handed off pre-validation for a live walkthrough.
ideation.problem_statement: The forked RealWorld app (nsidnev/fastapi-realworld-example-app, upstream commit 029eb7781c60d5f563ee8990a0cbfb79b244538c) models article comments as a flat, unordered list: each comment belongs to an article and an author only (see `app/db/repositories/commentaries.py` and the `commentaries` table), with no reply-to relationship and no way to tag another user inside a comment body. This blocks two concrete user needs: (1) replying to a specific existing comment so a conversation reads as a thread instead of a flat wall, and (2) @mentioning another user by username inside a comment so they can be made aware they were referenced. Neither capability exists today in the fork.
ideation.proposed_approach:
Extend the comments domain rather than introducing a new entity, to stay consistent with the existing RealWorld data model:

1. **Threading** — add a nullable self-referential `parent_comment_id` (FK to `commentaries.id`, same article) to the comment record. A comment with `parent_comment_id = null` is top-level; non-null makes it a reply. Depth is limited to one level (replies-to-top-level-comments only, no reply-to-reply nesting) — mirrors lightweight threading (e.g. GitHub PR review threads) rather than arbitrary-depth nesting.
2. **@Mentions** — parse the comment body for `@username` tokens at write time, resolve each against existing registered usernames (case-sensitive exact match, consistent with existing username lookups elsewhere in the fork), and persist resolved mentions as first-class records (`comment_id`, `mentioned_user_id`) rather than leaving them as unstructured text. Unresolved `@token`s are left as plain text, not linked, and do not error the request.
3. **API surface** — extend the existing comment create/response schema with `parent_comment_id` (optional on create, present on read) and a `mentions` array (username + user id) on the read response. Existing flat-list comment endpoints keep working unchanged for clients that ignore the new fields.
4. **Auth & error conventions** — all new/changed endpoints follow ADR 0001 (`Token` auth scheme, not `Bearer`; flat `{"errors": [...]}` error shape). E.g. replying to a nonexistent `parent_comment_id`, or replying to a comment on a different article than the URL's, returns a business-rule error via the existing flat-array shape.
5. **Notification delivery** — explicitly out of scope. `mentions` are persisted and readable via the API; active notification (email/in-app/websocket) is a separate concern for later.

Explicit stated assumptions (not left as silent ambiguity), carried forward unchanged from this feature's original scoping session with the user, which already confirmed this exact scope: one-level-deep threading only; mentions require an exact, case-sensitive existing username; unresolved mentions are silently left as plain text; no notification delivery in this pass.

scope_assessment.domains_justification: Touches two things within one service: a DB migration (new column + new table) and the FastAPI comment create/read routes + repository layer. No frontend, no separate service, no MCP changes — single bounded context (the comments domain of one backend).
scope_assessment.ambiguity_justification: Approach is fully pinned: one-level threading via nullable parent_comment_id, case-sensitive exact-match @mentions persisted to a join table, auth/error conventions inherited from ADR 0001. Minor details remain for refinement (exact regex character class for mention tokens, exact migration file naming per the fork's existing convention) but no open design question.
scope_assessment.dependencies_justification: Self-contained within the fork. No external API, no third-party service, no other team's component. Notification delivery (the one thing that could introduce a dependency) is explicitly out of scope for this pass.

## Parent Ideation Context
- Title: Threaded Replies + @Mentions for Article Comments
- Version: 6

### Description
Feature ideation for pulse-brownfield-feature-demo. Context: `app/` is a fresh fork of nsidnev/fastapi-realworld-example-app (FastAPI + Postgres RealWorld/Conduit clone), documented in `app/FORK_NOTES.md`. Auth/error conventions are documented in `docs/decisions/0001-token-auth-scheme.md`. This board was reset (prior ideation/refinement/spec/sprint/card chains hard-deleted) so this pipeline can be authored fresh and handed off pre-validation for a live walkthrough.

### Problem Statement
The forked RealWorld app (nsidnev/fastapi-realworld-example-app, upstream commit 029eb7781c60d5f563ee8990a0cbfb79b244538c) models article comments as a flat, unordered list: each comment belongs to an article and an author only (see `app/db/repositories/commentaries.py` and the `commentaries` table), with no reply-to relationship and no way to tag another user inside a comment body. 1. **Threading** — add a nullable self-referential `parent_comment_id` (FK to `commentaries.id`, same article) to the comment record. A comment with `parent_comment_id = null` is top-level; non-null makes it a reply. Depth is limited to one level (replies-to-top-level-comments only, no reply-to-reply nesting) — mirrors lightweight threading (e.g. GitHub PR review threads) rather than arbitrary-depth nesting.

3. **API surface** — extend the existing comment create/response schema with `parent_comment_id` (optional on create, present on read) and a `mentions` array (username + user id) on the read response. Explicit stated assumptions (not left as silent ambiguity), carried forward unchanged from this feature's original scoping session with the user, which already confirmed this exact scope: one-level-deep threading only; mentions require an exact, case-sensitive existing username; unresolved mentions are silently left as plain text; no notification delivery in this pass.

### Scope Assessment
- Domains: 2/5
- Ambiguity: 2/5
- Dependencies: 1/5
- Complexity: medium

functional_requirements.text: Users can create a comment as a reply to an existing top-level comment by supplying parent_comment_id, and the reply is persisted with that parent link.
Replying to a comment that is itself a reply (non-null parent_comment_id) is rejected — one-level-deep threading only.
Replying with a parent_comment_id belonging to a different article than the one in the request path is rejected.
Replying with a parent_comment_id that does not exist in the commentaries table is rejected.
@username tokens in a comment body are parsed and resolved against existing usernames via exact case-sensitive match, and resolved mentions are persisted as first-class records.
@username tokens that do not match any existing username remain as plain text in the comment body and do not cause the request to fail.
Every comment returned by GET or POST /articles/{slug}/comments includes parentCommentId and a mentions array reflecting persisted threading and mention state.

technical_requirements.text: New Alembic migration adds commentaries.parent_comment_id (INTEGER, NULL, FK->commentaries.id ON DELETE CASCADE), following the fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py create_*_table()/op.add_column convention.
New Alembic migration creates comment_mentions(comment_id FK->commentaries.id ON DELETE CASCADE, mentioned_user_id FK->users.id ON DELETE CASCADE) with UNIQUE(comment_id, mentioned_user_id).

Mention parsing uses a regex matching @ followed by valid username characters, resolved via a batched lookup reusing UsersRepository's existing exact-match pattern (app/db/repositories/users.py:17-26).

Only CommentInCreate/Comment schemas (app/models/schemas/comments.py, app/models/domain/comments.py) and CommentsRepository.create_comment_for_article (app/db/repositories/comments.py:61-78) are touched for the create path, plus the corresponding aiosql queries in app/db/queries/sql/comments.sql.
All new business-rule errors flow through the existing HTTPException -> http_error_handler flat {"errors": [...]} path (app/api/errors/http_error.py:6-7); no new error-handling middleware.

acceptance_criteria.text: Given an existing top-level comment on article X, when a user creates a comment on article X with parent_comment_id set to that comment's id, then the new comment is created and persisted with that parent_comment_id.

Given a comment that itself has a non-null parent_comment_id (a reply), when a user creates a comment with parent_comment_id set to that reply's id, then the request is rejected with a business-rule error and no comment is created.
Given a top-level comment on article Y, when a user creates a comment on article X (X != Y) with parent_comment_id set to that comment's id, then the request is rejected with a business-rule error.
Given a parent_comment_id that does not exist in the commentaries table, when a user creates a comment with that parent_comment_id, then the request is rejected with a business-rule error.

Given a registered user 'alice', when a comment body containing '@alice' is created, then a comment_mentions row (comment_id, alice's user id) is persisted and returned in the response's mentions array.

Given no registered user named 'nobody', when a comment body containing '@nobody' is created, then the comment is created successfully, '@nobody' remains as plain text in the body, and no comment_mentions row references it.

Given an existing comment with a parent and mentions, when GET /articles/{slug}/comments is called, then every comment in the response includes parentCommentId and a mentions array matching persisted state.

test_scenarios.title: Reply to a top-level comment persists parent link
test_scenarios.given: an existing top-level comment C1 on article "test-article" with parent_comment_id = null
test_scenarios.when: an authenticated user POSTs a comment to /articles/test-article/comments with body "nice point" and parent_comment_id = C1.id
test_scenarios.then: the response is 201 with the new comment's parentCommentId equal to C1.id, and GET /articles/test-article/comments subsequently returns it with the same parentCommentId

test_scenarios.title: Reply-to-a-reply is rejected
test_scenarios.given: a top-level comment C1 and a reply C2 with C2.parent_comment_id = C1.id
test_scenarios.when: a user POSTs a comment with parent_comment_id = C2.id
test_scenarios.then: the response is a business-rule error via the flat {"errors": [...]} shape, no comment is created, and the depth-limit rule fires

test_scenarios.title: Cross-article parent_comment_id is rejected
test_scenarios.given: a top-level comment C1 on article "article-y" and a different article "article-x"
test_scenarios.when: a user POSTs a comment to /articles/article-x/comments with parent_comment_id = C1.id
test_scenarios.then: the response is a business-rule error via the flat {"errors": [...]} shape and no comment is created

test_scenarios.title: Nonexistent parent_comment_id is rejected
test_scenarios.given: no comment exists with id 999999 on article "test-article"
test_scenarios.when: a user POSTs a comment to /articles/test-article/comments with parent_comment_id = 999999
test_scenarios.then: the response is a business-rule error via the flat {"errors": [...]} shape and no comment is created

test_scenarios.title: Mention of an existing user resolves and persists
test_scenarios.when: a user POSTs a comment with body "great work @alice" on any article
test_scenarios.then: a comment_mentions row (comment_id, alice's user id) is persisted, and the response's mentions array contains {"username": "alice", "id": alice.id}

test_scenarios.title: Mention of an unknown username does not error
test_scenarios.when: a user POSTs a comment with body "hey @nobody" on any article
test_scenarios.then: the response is 201, the body retains "@nobody" as plain text, and no comment_mentions row is created for it

test_scenarios.title: List comments includes threading and mentions on every row
test_scenarios.given: an article with one top-level comment, one reply to it, and one comment mentioning a registered user
test_scenarios.then: every comment in the response includes parentCommentId (null or the parent id) and a mentions array matching persisted comment_mentions state

business_rules.title: Reply persists with parent link
business_rules.rule: A comment created with a valid parent_comment_id is persisted with that parent link intact.
business_rules.when: a user creates a comment on article X with parent_comment_id set to an existing top-level comment on article X
business_rules.then: the comment is created and its parent_comment_id is persisted and returned on read

business_rules.title: Reply must target a top-level comment
business_rules.rule: One-level-deep threading is enforced: a reply cannot itself be replied to.
business_rules.when: a user creates a comment with parent_comment_id pointing at a comment whose own parent_comment_id is not null
business_rules.then: the request is rejected with a business-rule error via the flat {"errors": [...]} shape and no comment is created

business_rules.title: Reply must stay within the same article
business_rules.rule: A reply's parent comment must belong to the same article as the reply itself.
business_rules.when: a user creates a comment on article X with parent_comment_id pointing at a comment belonging to a different article
business_rules.then: the request is rejected with a business-rule error and no comment is created

business_rules.title: Reply target must exist
business_rules.rule: A parent_comment_id must reference an existing comment.
business_rules.when: a user creates a comment with a parent_comment_id that does not match any row in commentaries
business_rules.then: the request is rejected with a business-rule error and no comment is created

business_rules.title: Mentions resolve by exact username match
business_rules.rule: Only @tokens matching an existing username exactly (case-sensitive) are persisted as mentions.
business_rules.when: a comment body is parsed for @username tokens at create time
business_rules.then: each token matching an existing users.username exactly is persisted as a comment_mentions row referencing that user

business_rules.title: Unresolved mentions never error
business_rules.rule: A comment body containing an @token with no matching username is still accepted.
business_rules.when: an @token in the comment body does not match any existing username
business_rules.then: the token remains as plain text in the persisted body, no comment_mentions row is created for it, and the request succeeds

business_rules.title: Every comment response includes threading and mention data
business_rules.rule: parentCommentId and mentions are present on every serialized comment.
business_rules.when: a comment is serialized for a GET or POST /articles/{slug}/comments response
business_rules.then: the response includes parentCommentId (nullable) and a mentions array reflecting persisted comment_mentions rows

api_contracts.description: List all comments for an article, each including parentCommentId and mentions. Unchanged existing endpoint contract, extended with two additive fields.

decisions.title: Enforce depth-limit at the repository/service layer, not a DB constraint
decisions.rationale: Keeps the error message flowing through the existing flat-array HTTPException path (app/api/errors/http_error.py:6-7) instead of surfacing a raw asyncpg constraint-violation error, and matches how the codebase already validates business rules in Python (e.g. author-match checks) rather than in SQL.
decisions.context: Investigated by reading app/api/dependencies/comments.py's check_comment_modification_permissions pattern and app/api/errors/http_error.py.
alternatives_considered: A CHECK constraint or trigger enforcing depth in Postgres — discarded: would surface as an unhandled asyncpg IntegrityError rather than the expected flat {"errors": [...]} shape, breaking ADR 0001 consistency.

## Refinement Description
## Parent Ideation Context
- Title: Threaded Replies + @Mentions for Article Comments
- Version: 6

### Description
Feature ideation for pulse-brownfield-feature-demo. Context: `app/` is a fresh fork of nsidnev/fastapi-realworld-example-app (FastAPI + Postgres RealWorld/Conduit clone), documented in `app/FORK_NOTES.md`. Explicit stated assumptions (not left as silent ambiguity), carried forward unchanged from this feature's original scoping session with the user, which already confirmed this exact scope: one-level-deep threading only; mentions require an exact, case-sensitive existing username; unresolved mentions are silently left as plain text; no notification delivery in this pass.

### Scope Assessment
- Domains: 2/5
- Ambiguity: 2/5
- Dependencies: 1/5
- Complexity: medium

## In Scope
- Add nullable self-referential parent_comment_id (INTEGER, FK to commentaries.id, ON DELETE CASCADE) to the commentaries table via a new Alembic migration following the fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py create_*_table() convention
- Add a new comment_mentions table (comment_id FK->commentaries.id ON DELETE CASCADE, mentioned_user_id FK->users.id ON DELETE CASCADE) with a composite uniqueness constraint on (comment_id, mentioned_user_id)
- Extend CommentInCreate schema with optional parent_comment_id: Optional[int]
- Extend Comment domain model + response schema with parent_comment_id: Optional[int] and mentions: List[MentionedUser] (username + id)
- Validate on create: parent_comment_id must reference an existing comment on the SAME article, and that parent comment must itself be top-level (parent_comment_id IS NULL) to enforce one-level-deep threading
- Parse @username tokens from comment body at create time via regex, batch-resolve against users.username with exact case-sensitive match (reusing UsersRepository's existing lookup pattern), persist matches to comment_mentions
- Unresolved @tokens (no matching username) remain as plain text in body, are not persisted to comment_mentions, and do not error the request
- GET /articles/{slug}/comments and POST /articles/{slug}/comments both return parentCommentId and mentions on every comment in the response
- All new business-rule errors (nonexistent parent_comment_id, cross-article parent, reply-to-a-reply) use the existing flat {"errors": [...]} shape via the existing HTTPException/http_error_handler path

## Out of Scope
- Reply-to-reply / arbitrary-depth nesting — explicitly one level only per ideation assumption
- Active notification delivery (email/in-app/websocket) when mentioned — mentions are persisted and readable via API only
- Case-insensitive or fuzzy username matching for mentions
- Editing an existing comment to add/remove parent_comment_id or mentions after creation — no PATCH/PUT endpoint exists for comments today and none is being added
- Any frontend/UI work — this fork has no frontend component

## Analysis
**Source code (fork at `app/`, upstream commit 029eb7781c60d5f563ee8990a0cbfb79b244538c):**

- `app/db/migrations/versions/fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py:167-194` — `create_commentaries_table()` defines the current schema: `commentaries(id, body, author_id FK->users.id ON DELETE CASCADE, article_id FK->articles.id ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at, updated_at)`. No self-reference, no mentions table. The file's per-table `create_*_table()` helper-function convention (one function per table, called from `upgrade()`) is the pattern a new migration must follow.
- `app/db/queries/sql/comments.sql:20-34` — aiosql-style named queries. `create-new-comment<!` does `WITH users_subquery AS (SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username = :author_username) INSERT INTO commentaries (...) RETURNING ...` — confirms username lookup is exact-string `WHERE username = :value`, no case-insensitive collation, matching the case-sensitive-mention assumption.
- `app/db/repositories/comments.py:61-78` — `CommentsRepository.create_comment_for_article()` is the single write path for comment creation; calls `queries.create_new_comment` and maps the row via `_get_comment_from_db_record` (line 87). Any `parent_comment_id`/mention handling must be added here.
- `app/models/domain/comments.py:6-8` — `Comment(IDModelMixin, DateTimeModelMixin, RWModel)` has only `body: str` and `author: Profile`. No `parent_comment_id` or `mentions` field exists.
- `app/models/schemas/comments.py:15-16` — `CommentInCreate(RWSchema)` has only `body: str`. This is the request schema `POST /articles/{slug}/comments` binds to (via `app/api/routes/comments.py:47`, `Body(..., embed=True, alias="comment")`).
- `app/api/routes/comments.py:26-57` — `list_comments_for_article` (GET) and `create_comment_for_article` (POST) are the two endpoints in scope. Both depend on `get_repository(CommentsRepository)`. No route changes needed beyond schema fields — routing/dependency wiring stays the same.
- `app/db/repositories/users.py:17-26` — `UsersRepository.get_user_by_username()` is the existing exact-match username lookup pattern; mention resolution should reuse this same repository rather than a bespoke query.
- `app/api/errors/http_error.py:6-7` — confirms `{"errors": [exc.detail]}` flat-array shape for all `HTTPException`s (business-rule errors). Matches ADR 0001.

**Knowledge Graph (Stage 2 query set, run before this refinement moved to approved):** `okto_pulse_kg_find_similar_decisions` (topic: comment threading data model / mention resolution) returned 0 hits; `okto_pulse_kg_find_contradictions` (board-wide, no existing decisions to anchor on) returned 0 pairs. `okto_pulse_kg_list_alternatives` not applicable — no existing decision node to query alternatives for; this refinement is the first decision recorded on this board (the board was reset — see ideation description). No prior art to extend or contradict.

**Web research:** not required — no third-party library/protocol dependency is introduced (Alembic and aiosql are already in use and unchanged in usage pattern).

**Stakeholder context:** the exact scope (one-level threading, case-sensitive exact-match mentions, no notification delivery) was already explicitly stated as assumptions in the parent ideation and is carried forward unchanged; no open Q&A exists on the ideation.

## Decisions
- Extend the existing commentaries table with a nullable self-referential FK rather than introducing a separate threads/replies entity — matches the existing RealWorld data model's convention of flat tables with FKs (see favorites, articles_to_tags as precedent for join-table style) and requires no new domain concept. No prior KG decision exists to extend or supersede (board reset, zero prior nodes) — this is new knowledge, not a reuse.
- Depth-limit enforcement (one level only) happens at the repository/service layer on create, not as a DB CHECK constraint — consistent with how the existing codebase validates business rules in Python (e.g. comment-author-matches-check in check_comment_modification_permissions) rather than in SQL constraints, and keeps the error message flowing through the existing flat-array HTTPException path instead of a raw asyncpg constraint-violation error.
- Mentions persist as a separate comment_mentions join table rather than a JSON/array column on commentaries — enables a straightforward FK to users.id (referential integrity, cascade delete) and a simple indexed lookup, matching the existing join-table pattern (favorites, articles_to_tags, followers_to_followings) already established in fdf8821871d7_main_tables.py.
